content: Specialization of FormulaExpression These specializations represent three kinds of extensions: • The applicable operands are specified as associations in the subclasses (see [TPS_GST_00001] for more details). The valid reference in the grammar be- low are taken from the role names in the meta model. Maintaining the references as formal associations allows to retrieve dependencies even without parsing the formula expressions. • Additional functions are represented by the specialization and documented in the context of the same (see [TPS_GST_00293] for more details). It is not possible to extend the language by further operators. • The particular application constrains the expected result. E.g. in Attribute- ValueVariationPoint , the result is given by the type of the variant attribute. Another example is swSyscond which expects a boolean result.
